# SHABM (شبم) — BAGHDAD OPERATING COST STACK
## Research dimension: the inputs to a P&L
**Compiled 22 August 2026. FX basis: IQD 1,320 = USD 1.00 (Central Bank of Iraq official rate, unchanged since February 2023).**

---

## 0. METHOD, AND AN HONEST NOTE ON SOURCE QUALITY

Read this section before you put any of these numbers in front of an investor.

**What happened during this research.** Direct page-fetching (WebFetch and curl) was blocked at the network egress layer for essentially every target domain — OpenSooq Iraq, aiqarat.com, Shafaq News, Al-Rasheed Media, Wikipedia, PwC Tax Summaries, Numbeo, GlobalPetrolPrices, Al Tamimi, WageIndicator, Telegram job channels. The session's shared web-search budget was then exhausted (200/200 calls) partway through the COGS block. Consequently:

- Figures below marked **[SOURCED]** were extracted from search-engine result summaries of the named pages. They are real published figures with named publishers and dates, but **I could not open the underlying page to verify context, units, or whether the number was superseded.** Treat them as high-quality leads, not audited facts.
- Figures marked **[ESTIMATE]** are my own derivations. Every one carries its reasoning so you can attack it.
- The weakest block in this report is **fruit wholesale pricing (§5.4)** and **mall kiosk rent (§1.2)**. Both need a physical check in Baghdad before they go in a model. I flag them loudly rather than dressing them up.

**Confidence tiering used throughout:**
- **HIGH** — figure from a named institution/publisher, 2023–2026, internally cross-checked
- **MEDIUM** — single published source, or a derivation from HIGH inputs
- **LOW** — my estimate from structural reasoning; needs field verification

**A cross-check on the FX rate.** Three independent data points in this research triangulate the rate, which gives some confidence the conversions are sound: commercial electricity quoted at both IQD 60/kWh and USD 0.046/kWh implies 1,304; Baghdad milk quoted at both IQD 1,600 and USD 1.20 implies 1,333; Numbeo's own milk figure of IQD 1,588. All cluster at 1,300–1,335. I use **1,320**. Note that Iraq has historically run a parallel/black-market USD rate above the official peg; I was unable to source a current 2026 parallel rate in this session and flag it as an open question (§Open Questions), because if you pay rent in USD cash and earn revenue in IQD, the spread is a real and unhedged cost.

---

## 1. COMMERCIAL RENT IN BAGHDAD

### 1.1 Street-front shops — Mansour / Karrada / Zayouna

**Hard listing comparables found (all live listings on aiqarat.com "عقارات العراق", surfaced 2025–2026):**

| Location | Type | Area | Monthly rent | Derived $/m²/month |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mansour, 14 Ramadan Street | محل (shop) | 350 m² | **USD 3,500** | $10.00 |
| Zayouna, near Dream Mall | دار تجاري (commercial house) | 200 m² | **USD 5,500** | $27.50 |
| Zayouna | مشتمل (annexe unit) | 50 m² | **IQD 1,100,000** (≈$833) | $16.67 |
| Karrada | shop | n/a | **USD 1,000/mo + USD 25,000 خلو** | — |
| Karrada | commercial office | n/a | **IQD 300,000** (≈$227) | — |
| Mansour | furnished apartment (context anchor) | 150 m² | USD 1,300 | $8.67 |
| Mansour | commercial building, **for sale** | 310 m² | rental income USD 12,000/mo; sale $14,000/m² | $38.71 income yield basis |

*[SOURCED — aiqarat.com listings; MEDIUM confidence. These are asking prices, not transacted prices. Iraqi asking rents typically negotiate down 10–20%.]*

**Reading the comparables.** Two structural facts jump out:

1. **Per-m² rent falls sharply with size.** The 350 m² Mansour unit at $10/m² and the 200 m² Zayouna unit at $27.50/m² bracket the market. Large-format units are cheap per metre because the tenant pool is thin. **Small units are the expensive ones per metre** — the opposite of what a naive model assumes.
2. **Zayouna near Dream Mall is roughly 2.75× Mansour 14 Ramadan on a per-m² basis.** Micro-location dominates; "Mansour" or "Karrada" as a district label is not a rent input, the specific street is.

**14 Ramadan Street** (Mansour) and **Karrada Dakhil / Karrada Kharij** are Baghdad's established F&B and retail strips; **Zayouna** near Dream Mall has become the high-footfall young-consumer strip, which is why it prices highest.

**ESTIMATE — 30–60 m² prime street-front, Mansour / Karrada / Zayouna:**

| Scenario | $/m²/month | 30 m² | 45 m² | 60 m² |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secondary street, off-pitch | $18 | $540 | $810 | $1,080 |
| Good street, solid footfall | $30 | $900 | $1,350 | $1,800 |
| Prime pitch (14 Ramadan, Karrada Dakhil, Zayouna nr Dream Mall) | $45–55 | $1,350–1,650 | $2,025–2,475 | $2,700–3,300 |

*[ESTIMATE — LOW-MEDIUM confidence. **Derivation:** the two sourced small-format anchors are the 50 m² Zayouna unit at $16.67/m² (an annexe, not street-front retail — so a floor) and the 200 m² Zayouna commercial house at $27.50/m² (prime location, but large format — so also a floor for small format at the same pitch). Applying a standard small-unit premium of 1.5–2.0× to the $27.50 prime large-format rate gives $41–55/m² for a 30–60 m² prime street-front box. The Karrada listing at $1,000/month independently corroborates the middle of this range for a typical (not prime) small shop.]*

**Planning number for the SHABM model: USD 1,400–1,800/month (IQD 1.85m–2.38m) for a ~50 m² prime-adjacent street-front unit; USD 2,400–3,000/month if you insist on a true trophy pitch.**

**Recommendation for the deck:** SHABM's brand concept is a *giant transparent ice cube on the pavement*. That is a visibility-driven, impulse-purchase format. It argues for paying the prime-pitch premium rather than economising — but it also argues for taking the **smallest viable footprint** at that pitch, because rent scales with metres and the brand value scales with the façade. A 35–40 m² unit with a 6–8 m frontage beats a 70 m² unit with a 4 m frontage at the same total rent.

### 1.2 Mall kiosks — Baghdad Mall / Mansour Mall / Al-Mansour City Center

**I could not source a single verified Baghdad mall kiosk rate.** This is a genuine gap. Mall leasing in Iraq is negotiated privately, rates are not published, and the listing portals do not carry in-mall units. Do not let this gap be papered over in the deck.

**[ESTIMATE — LOW confidence. Structural reasoning:]** Regional mall leasing in MENA for a 15–25 m² food kiosk/RMU typically prices on one of three structures:

1. **Base rent per m²**, at a 2–4× premium to street rent for the same city, reflecting captive footfall, security, and A/C included. Baghdad street prime at ~$45/m² → mall kiosk **$90–150/m²/month** → a 20 m² kiosk at **$1,800–3,000/month**.
2. **Turnover rent** — a percentage of gross sales, commonly **10–18%** for F&B kiosks in MENA malls, sometimes with a minimum guaranteed rent (MGR) floor.
3. **Base + percentage** — the most common in newer malls: a base at ~60–70% of the pure-base figure, plus 6–10% of turnover above a breakpoint.

Plus, almost universally: a **service charge / common area maintenance (CAM)** of roughly **$15–30/m²/month** covering mall A/C, security, cleaning and marketing — which in Baghdad, where the mall supplies reliable generator-backed power and cooling, is genuinely valuable and materially de-risks §3.

**Planning number: USD 1,800–3,000/month all-in (rent + CAM) for a 20 m² kiosk, or negotiate to 12–15% of turnover with a low MGR.**

**Strategic note.** For SHABM specifically, the mall kiosk is arguably the *stronger* first unit despite similar rent, for three reasons the cost stack itself reveals: (a) mall CAM absorbs the brutal §3 power and cooling problem, which is SHABM's single largest controllable risk; (b) mall A/C means the "ice cube" façade doesn't fight 50°C ambient; (c) the biggest cost line — labour (§2) — is lower because a kiosk runs 3 staff instead of 8. The street-front flagship is the brand statement; the kiosk is the unit economics.

### 1.3 Key money — خلو / goodwill

**How it works in Iraq.** خلو (khulū, "key money" / goodwill) is a lump sum paid **up front and non-refundably**, usually to the *outgoing tenant* rather than the landlord, to acquire the right to occupy a commercial unit. It is entirely separate from rent, from any deposit, and from fixtures.

**Observed magnitude [SOURCED — MEDIUM]:** a Karrada shop listed at **USD 1,000/month rent with USD 25,000 خلو**. That is a ratio of **25× monthly rent**, or **~2.1 years of rent paid up front and never recovered.**

**The legal position, which matters.** Iraq's **Property Lease Law No. 87 of 1979** (as amended, published by the Iraqi General Commission for Taxes / Ministry of Finance at tax.mof.gov.iq) contains an express prohibition: *"لا يجوز للمؤجر أو المستأجر أو الوسيط أو أي شخص آخر أن يحصل على أي مال أو منفعة خارج نطاق عقد الإيجار"* — neither landlord, tenant, broker, nor any other person may obtain any money or benefit outside the scope of the lease contract. **[SOURCED — HIGH; primary legislation, Iraqi Ministry of Finance]**

So khulū is, on its face, **unlawful under the lease statute — and simultaneously near-universal in practice.** The practical consequences for SHABM:

- The payment is typically **undocumented or documented as something else** (sale of fixtures, sale of a "business"). It is therefore **not enforceable, not recoverable, and not a clean balance-sheet asset.**
- It cannot be reliably written into a franchise agreement as a recoverable item.
- It creates a **real exit risk**: you recover khulū only by finding the next tenant willing to pay it, which depends on the pitch still being desirable in 3–5 years.
- Iraqi commercial leases are governed differently from residential ones, and the **eviction position of a commercial tenant is a live litigation area** (see Iraqi Lawyers Network, "الفرق بين الإيجار التجاري والسكني في العراق" and "إخلاء المستأجر من العقار التجاري في العراق"). Commercial leases end on expiry and renew only by mutual agreement. **[SOURCED — MEDIUM]**

**Modelling treatment [ESTIMATE — MEDIUM]:**
- Budget **khulū of 15–30× monthly rent** for a good pitch; **USD 20,000–45,000** for the target street-front unit. Prime 14 Ramadan or Karrada Dakhil pitches can run higher.
- Many mall kiosks charge **no khulū** — another point in the kiosk's favour, and a material one: it is $25k+ of capital not sunk into an unenforceable payment.
- In the model, treat khulū as **capex amortised over the lease term** (5 years → ~$417/month on a $25,000 payment), and **separately disclose it as an at-risk, legally unenforceable outlay.** An investor who knows Iraq will ask; one who doesn't needs to be told.

### 2.4 Social security — employer cost

**Workers' Retirement and Social Security Law No. 18 of 2023**, published in Official Gazette **No. 4734 on 28 August 2023**, in force from **1 December 2023**. **[SOURCED — HIGH; Al Tamimi & Co., Deloitte Middle East, WTW, Lexis Middle East, HHL Iraq]**

| Contribution | Rate | Payer |
|---|---|---|
| **Base contribution** | **17% of wages** | split **12% employer / 5% employee** |
| Private/mixed sector, oil & gas and related | **25%** | employer (does not apply to SHABM) |
| **Additional 8%** | 8% | **Government pays it for Iraqi national employees.** Employer pays it for **expatriate** employees registered for SSPC purposes |

**Modelling rule for SHABM: employer social security = 12% of gross payroll**, provided the workforce is Iraqi nationals. **If you hire an expatriate head barista or Japanese ice-carving trainer on the payroll, that individual costs 12% + 8% = 20%.** That is a real and often-missed cost of importing the specialist skill the concept depends on — worth structuring as a short-term consultancy/training engagement rather than employment.

### 2.5 Working hours and the one-vs-two shift question

**Statutory position [ESTIMATE — MEDIUM, from general knowledge of Labour Law No. 37 of 2015; I could not open a source to verify]:** standard working time is **8 hours/day, 48 hours/week**, with overtime premia and a weekly rest day.

**Observed market practice [SOURCED — MEDIUM-HIGH]:** the postings tell a clear and different story.

- Café Diva advertises **17:00–01:00** — an 8-hour single evening shift.
- Chef assistant: **evening shift from 17:00**.
- The market distinguishes **"دوام كامل" (full shift) at IQD 750,000** from **"evening shift" at IQD 450,000** — a wage ratio of **1.67×**.

**The inference that matters.** If "full shift" were simply two 8-hour shifts' worth of work, the ratio would be ~2.0×. At 1.67× it points to a **long single shift of roughly 12–14 hours** — the Baghdad F&B norm — rather than a two-shift rotation. **Baghdad F&B predominantly runs ONE long shift, topped up by a cheaper evening-only crew for the peak.** Two-shift rotation is the exception, used by larger organised chains.

**Two consequences for SHABM, both favourable:**

1. **The peak is cheap.** Baghdad's social life — and any cold-drinks business — peaks in the evening, after the heat breaks. That is precisely when the marginal labour hour costs IQD 450,000/month rather than IQD 750,000. Staff the peak with evening crew and the labour line falls without touching service quality at the hours that generate revenue.
2. **Compliance risk to disclose.** A 12–14 hour shift **exceeds the statutory 8-hour day.** Market practice and the Labour Law diverge, and enforcement is weak — but a franchisor selling a system across Iraq and then into Saudi, UAE and Qatar (where enforcement is *not* weak) should build a compliant two-shift model into the franchise operations manual from day one, and price it. Do not export a non-compliant labour model into the GCC.

## 3. UTILITIES AND POWER — THE CRITICAL LINE FOR THIS BUSINESS

This section deserves the most attention in the deck, because SHABM is simultaneously (a) a heavy-refrigeration business, (b) in a 50°C summer city, (c) on a broken grid, (d) behind a fully glazed façade. Those four facts compound.

### 3.1 Grid tariff

| Tariff | Rate | Source | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Residential, federal Iraq** | **IQD 10/kWh** (≈ USD 0.008) | Iraq Business News, *"No Change to Iraq's Subsidised Electricity Prices"*, **10 December 2025**. State covers **>65% of production cost** | HIGH |
| **Commercial, federal Iraq** | **IQD 60/kWh** (≈ USD 0.046) | GlobalPetrolPrices.com, **June 2025** | MEDIUM-HIGH |
| KRG commercial (comparison) | IQD 185/kWh | KRG Ministry of Electricity, Project Runaki tariff, **May 2025** (gov.krd) | HIGH |

**Federal Baghdad commercial power at IQD 60/kWh (USD 0.046) is among the cheapest in the world.** Iraq has been ranked among the top 11 countries globally for cheapest electricity (Shafaq News). **The grid is not the problem. The grid's availability is.**

**Model assumption: grid available ~10 h/day (42% of hours); private generation must cover the other ~14 h/day (58%).**

### 3.3 Neighbourhood generator (المولدة) — the ampere subscription

Baghdad Provincial Council **sets the ampere tariff monthly by decree.** This is unusually well-documented and is HIGH-confidence data.

| Month | "Golden" / 24-hour operation | Night operation | Privatised areas | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **August 2025** | **IQD 12,000/ampere** (generators receiving fuel allocation) | — | — | Baghdad Today; Al-Mawrid News |
| **September 2025** | **IQD 12,000/ampere** (alternating with national grid) | — | — | Al-Rasheed TV, 7 Sept 2025; Wakalat Al-Sahafa Al-Mustaqila |
| **October 2025** | **IQD 9,000/ampere / 24 h** | **IQD 7,000/ampere** (13:00–06:00) | — | Al-Rasheed TV, 3 Oct 2025 |
| **June 2026** | **IQD 12,000/ampere** | **IQD 8,000/ampere** | **IQD 6,000/ampere** | Shafaq News |

**[SOURCED — HIGH; these are published municipal decrees]**

**Clear seasonal pattern: IQD 12,000/ampere in summer operating months, falling to ~IQD 9,000 as the summer operating season ends.** Households pay **USD 100–300/month** in total for generator supply (Shafaq News / Middle East Monitor).

**Deriving the effective cost per kWh from the ampere tariff — a number you will need:**

An "ampere" in the Iraqi generator market is reckoned at ~220 V, i.e. **1 A ≈ 0.22 kW** of entitlement.

- At **full 24 h/day draw**: 0.22 kW × 720 h = 158.4 kWh/month → IQD 12,000 ÷ 158.4 = **IQD 76/kWh**
- At **realistic 14 h/day generator running** (grid off): 0.22 × 14 × 30 = 92.4 kWh → **IQD 130/kWh**

*[ESTIMATE — MEDIUM; derivation shown]*

**This is a genuinely important insight for SHABM.** Households draw their subscribed ampere intermittently, so their effective rate is poor (IQD 150–250/kWh). **SHABM's load is dominated by refrigeration, which runs continuously.** A near-100% load factor means SHABM extracts far more kWh per subscribed ampere than a household does — **the ampere subscription is structurally cheaper for this business than for the neighbours paying the same tariff.** That is a defensible cost advantage worth stating in the deck.

### 3.4 Private diesel generator — the alternative

| Item | Value | Source | Confidence |

| **Diesel price, Iraq** | **USD 0.190/litre ≈ IQD 251/litre** | GlobalPetrolPrices.com, **July 2026** | MEDIUM-HIGH |
| Gasoline 95, Baghdad (context) | IQD 850/litre | GlobalPetrolPrices.com, avg 24 Nov 2025 – 2 Mar 2026 | MEDIUM |

**Derived cost of self-generated power [ESTIMATE — MEDIUM]:**
- A diesel genset at typical partial load consumes **0.28–0.35 litre/kWh**; use **0.30**.
- 0.30 l/kWh × IQD 251/l = **IQD 75/kWh fuel**
- Plus oil, filters, servicing at ~20% of fuel cost → **IQD 90/kWh ≈ USD 0.068/kWh** all-in running cost, excluding genset capex.

**Note the convergence: IQD 76/kWh (ampere subscription at full draw) vs IQD 90/kWh (own genset).** The two routes cost nearly the same per kWh. The decision is therefore **not** about price — it is about **capex, reliability and control**:
- **المولدة subscription**: zero capex, zero maintenance, but you are hostage to the operator's run hours and to a load cap. **A neighbourhood generator will generally not sell a single subscriber 40–70 amperes.**
- **Own genset**: ~$4,000–9,000 capex for a 20–30 kVA unit (ESTIMATE), plus fuel logistics and a place to put it, but full control — and for a business where a -80°C freezer failure destroys inventory and a day's ice-block production, **control is the point.**

**Recommendation: own genset with automatic transfer switch as primary backup, plus a المولدة subscription as a secondary fallback.** Redundancy here is not gold-plating; it is inventory insurance.

**Blended cost of electricity for the model [ESTIMATE — MEDIUM]:**
42% grid @ IQD 60 + 58% generator @ IQD 90 = **IQD 77/kWh ≈ USD 0.058/kWh blended.**

### 3.6 The ice-cube façade problem — quantified

**This is the single most important cost finding in this report, and it comes directly from the brand concept.**

SHABM's identity is a **giant transparent ice cube**. Executed literally in single glazing, in Baghdad:

- Solar heat gain through single glazing in Baghdad summer: **500–700 W/m²** at peak.
- A 50 m² unit with ~30 m² of sun-facing glazing: **30 × 600 W = 18 kW of solar gain from the glass alone** — that is **5 tons of cooling just to stand still against the façade.**
- Add heat rejected into the space by the refrigeration stack (~8–10 kW), plus occupants and fabric → **total cooling load 30–35 kW ≈ 8.5–10 tons.**
- At COP 2.8 → **11–12.5 kW electrical**, running 16 h/day at 75% duty → **132–150 kWh/day for A/C alone in peak summer** — roughly **double** the conventional-envelope assumption above.

| Scenario | Summer kWh/day | Summer monthly kWh |
|---|---|---|
| Conventional envelope, modest glazing | ~230 | ~6,900 |
| **Literal single-glazed ice-cube façade** | **~300–310** | **~9,000–9,300** |

**Mitigation and its value.** Double-glazed low-E insulated glass units (IGUs) cut solar gain by **50–60%**. That recovers roughly **60–75 kWh/day** in summer — worth about **IQD 4,600–5,800/day ≈ USD 105–130/month** in peak season, and it materially reduces the required genset size and A/C capex.

**The deck line:** *the brand concept is the biggest single driver of the utility bill, and specifying insulated glazing at fit-out is what makes the concept affordable to run.* Frame it as a design decision with a quantified payback, not as a cost overrun. It also happens to be the correct answer aesthetically — low-E IGU reads as thicker, bluer, more genuinely ice-like than single glazing.

Iraq is a **first-to-file** jurisdiction in practice.
2. **A franchise business cannot license what it does not own.** The trademark *is* the franchisable asset. Every regional expansion target named in the plan — Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt, Qatar, Kuwait, Jordan — needs its own filing, and most are Madrid Protocol members while **Iraq is not**, so Iraqi filing must be direct and national filings elsewhere must be handled separately. Budget **USD 12,000–25,000** for a six-market regional trademark portfolio across three classes. *[ESTIMATE — LOW]*

Also register the **Arabic script mark (شبم) separately from the Latin mark (SHABM)** — they are distinct marks and a single filing does not protect both.

## 9. THE FIVE THINGS THAT MOVE THIS MODEL MOST

Ranked by the size of the swing they create, so the deck can address them head-on:

1. **Labour, at 59% of fixed cost.** Not rent. The evening-shift wage arbitrage (IQD 450k vs 750k) sits exactly on top of peak demand and is the highest-leverage operating decision available.
2. **The glazed façade's cooling load.** The brand concept drives the utility bill. Single glazing vs low-E IGU is a **USD 105–130/month** swing in peak season plus a materially larger genset and A/C capex. Specify insulated glazing at fit-out; it is both the cheaper and the better-looking answer.
3. **Fruit seasonality on the sorbet line.** Strawberry swings 3–4× between February–May and the rest of the year; blackberry may never work. **The blast-freezer and ULT capex already in the plan doubles as a procurement hedge** — buy at season, freeze, hold. This is a real and defensible advantage over a conventional café.
4. **Key money at USD 25,000, legally unenforceable.** Under Property Lease Law No. 87 of 1979 it is prohibited and therefore unrecoverable. Disclose it. The mall-kiosk route avoids it entirely.
5. **Trademark lead time of 12–24 months.** The longest pole in the tent for a business whose value is the brand and whose plan is to franchise. File in classes 30, 32 and 43, in both Latin and Arabic script, **before** launch.

## 10. WHAT AN INVESTOR WILL CHECK, AND WHAT WILL NOT SURVIVE

Be candid about this in the data room rather than being caught out:

**Will survive scrutiny (HIGH confidence, primary or institutional sources):**
- Minimum wage IQD 350,000 (Labour Law 37/2015)
- Social security 12% employer / 5% employee (Law 18/2023, Gazette 4734)
- Electricity tariffs IQD 10 residential / IQD 60 commercial; grid 8–12 h/day
- Generator ampere tariffs IQD 6,000–12,000 (published monthly by Baghdad Provincial Council)
- Diesel USD 0.190/litre
- Corporate income tax 15%; no general VAT; 10% sales tax on deluxe restaurants
- LLC minimum capital IQD 1,000,000; 6–10 weeks to register
- Trademark: 10-year term, 12–24 month pendency, Industrial Property Directorate

**Needs field verification before the raise (LOW confidence):**
- **Mall kiosk rent** — no verified Baghdad data exists in this research. Get three written quotes from Baghdad Mall, Mansour Mall and Al-Mansour City Center.
- **Fruit wholesale prices** — check **alwaiq.com** and walk **علوة جميلة** in person. Photograph the price board.
- **Sugar, cream, stabiliser, PET cup pricing** — get supplier quotes with MOQs.
- **Municipal and health licence fees** — no published schedule; ask Amanat Baghdad directly.
- **LLC registration official fees** — get a quote from Iraqi corporate counsel.
- **Aggregator status and rates** — confirm whether Talabat currently operates in Iraq at all, and get Lezzoo's actual merchant rate card.
- **The IQD parallel-market rate** — if rent is paid in USD cash and revenue earned in IQD, the spread is an unhedged cost this model does not yet capture.

**The honest framing for the deck:** the *structural* cost drivers — labour, power, tax, licensing — are well-sourced and stable, and they say this business works at 55–93 covers a day. The *procurement* details are estimates that a week in Baghdad will nail down. That is the right order of confidence for a pre-launch plan, and saying so plainly will build more credibility with a serious investor than false precision would.

Source the current parallel rate and add an FX sensitivity.

MUNICIPAL TRADE LICENCE AND HEALTH LICENCE FEES — no published fee schedule exists for either the إجازة ممارسة مهنة or the الإجازة الصحية للمحل العام. The regulatory requirement is confirmed by primary legislation but the cost is a pure estimate (IQD 250,000-1,500,000/year). Ask Amanat Baghdad directly, and check the new 'Ur' national portal e-licensing service which may compress timelines.

OFFICIAL LLC REGISTRATION FEES — the IQD 1,000,000 minimum capital and 6-10 week timeline are well-sourced, but the actual registrar/notary/gazette fee schedule is not published anywhere accessible. Get a fixed-fee quote from Iraqi corporate counsel.

CURRENT IRAQI TRADEMARK OFFICE FEE SCHEDULE — sources confirm the office recently introduced a revised official fee structure following a legislative decision, but the new amounts are not public. The USD 300-600/class figure may be superseded. Confirm with a local IP agent before budgeting the regional portfolio.

SALES TAX CLASSIFICATION — the 10% sales tax applies to 'deluxe restaurants and first-class hotels'. Whether a premium-positioned café/kiosk falls inside that administrative classification is a 10-point-of-revenue question. Obtain a written opinion from Iraqi tax counsel before the raise closes; model both cases.

SUGAR, CREAM, STABILISER AND PET PACKAGING PRICING — all unsourced (budget expired). Get Baghdad supplier quotes with MOQs, particularly for custom-printed PET, where minimums of 10,000-50,000 units will drive an early working-capital call.

BAGHDAD RO/POTABLE WATER PRICING — no per-unit prices obtainable. The IQD 250-500 per 20-litre jerry can figure is an unverified estimate. Note the recommendation is to install in-house commercial RO regardless, since low-TDS water is a technical prerequisite for clear ice-block carving, not merely a cost choice.

STATUTORY WORKING HOURS UNDER LABOUR LAW 37/2015 — the 8h/day, 48h/week standard could not be sourced directly. Verify. This matters because observed Baghdad F&B practice (12-14 hour single shifts) appears to exceed the statutory limit, which is a compliance exposure that must be resolved before exporting the operating model into GCC markets where enforcement is real.

COMMERCIAL DIESEL PROCUREMENT PRICE — the USD 0.190/litre pump price is the subsidised rate. Generators and businesses buying outside the official allocation frequently pay a premium. Establish the actual delivered price a commercial subscriber pays in Baghdad, and confirm whether the July-August free-diesel allocation (45 litres per 1 kVA) extends to private commercial gensets or only to neighbourhood generator operators.

ULT FREEZER AND CLEAR-ICE MACHINE CAPEX AND SERVICE AVAILABILITY IN IRAQ — outside this dimension's scope but adjacent to it: confirm that -80°C ULT freezers and directional-freeze (Clinebell-type) clear-ice machines can be imported, serviced and supplied with spare parts in Baghdad. A refrigeration failure with no local service engineer destroys inventory and halts the two highest-margin product lines.
